unit: Mrs. Allan is a close friend and trusted confidante to Anne Shirley, offering her gentle comfort and encouraging advice throughout her youth and early adulthood. Their friendship begins when Mrs. Allan gracefully forgives Anne for accidentally serving her a cake flavored with liniment, choosing to comfort the embarrassed girl and admire her garden instead. Over the years, Mrs. Allan supports Anne through major life transitions, helping her process her grief after Matthew's sudden death and advising her on teaching and ideals.

label: Appearance
value: Anne is a slender girl.
unit: Anne is a slender girl with a pointed, freckled face and pale skin. She has solemn, luminous gray eyes that can shine like stars or swell with big tears, along with a pretty nose featuring seven distinct freckles. Noted for her skinny, thin build, she has long red hair—also described as auburn or Titian—which she wears in braids or leaves streaming. At one point, her hair was accidentally dyed green.

label: Personality
value: Anne aims to attend Redmond College.
unit: Driven by her aspirations, she aims to attend Redmond College and win the Thorburn Scholarship in English, hoping to gain knowledge on how to live life best, add beauty to the world, and eventually write a story good enough for publication. Her long-term goal after finishing college is to stick to teaching, having previously wanted to pass her examinations high for Matthew's sake and work hard to win the Avery scholarship. Characterized as talkative, passionate, and romantic, she possesses an intense imagination, though this high degree of daydreaming combined with a heedless and impulsive nature often leaves her forgetful and prone to making mistakes. She harbors a notable vanity regarding her long, thick, curly red hair, and she deeply fears traversing the Haunted Wood after dark due to terrors of white things grabbing her. Possessing a natural knack and fondness for children, she is exceptionally skilled at nursing and treating young children with croup, while also seeking to win over a young student like Anthony Pye. Additionally, she demonstrates talent in rowing a dory, writing compositions, decorating artistically, public recitation, singing with a good voice, and imaginative storytelling.

label: History
value: Anne Shirley was born in Bolingbroke, Nova Scotia.
unit: Born in Bolingbroke, Nova Scotia, Anne Shirley lost her parents in early infancy and spent her early childhood moving between guardians and an asylum [F2, F3, F4, F5, F9, F13]. At eleven years old, she was brought to Prince Edward Island by Mrs. Spencer, where Matthew and Marilla Cuthbert ultimately decided to adopt her at Green Gables [F12, S1, S3, S5]. She quickly swore an oath of lifelong friendship with Diana Barry and developed a fierce, long-standing rivalry with Gilbert Blythe after he pulled her hair at school [S9, S13]. Following years of local schooling and attending Queen's Academy, she gave up her college scholarship to remain at Green Gables after Matthew died, working as the Avonlea teacher to support Marilla [S40, S42, S43]. During her tenure as a teacher, she helped Marilla raise the orphaned twins Davy and Dora Keith while actively participating in the Avonlea Village Improvement Society [S49, S52]. Later, Anne left for Redmond College to pursue her degree, moving into a charming house called Patty's Place with her friends Priscilla, Phil, and Stella [S81, S85, S89, S95]. Throughout her college years, she received and rejected multiple marriage proposals, including an awkward proxy proposal from Jane Andrews on behalf of her brother Billy, as well as an earnest declaration from Gilbert [S87, S100]. Although she spent months courted by Roy Gardner, she ultimately turned down his proposal after realizing she did not love him [S103, S114]. Upon returning to Avonlea after graduation, she discovered that Gilbert had not engaged Christine Stuart as rumored [S113, S116]. Walking together to Hester Gray's garden, Gilbert proposed once more, and Anne joyfully accepted, ending their long misunderstandings and becoming engaged [S116].

label: Quote
value: Anne Shirley said: "Pretty well. I’m better at looking after children, though. I’ve had so much experience at that. It’s such a pity you haven’t any here for me to look after."

label: Quote
value: Anne Shirley said: “I think he’s lovely,” said Anne reproachfully. “He is so very sympathetic. He didn’t mind how much I talked—he seemed to like it. I felt that he was a kindred spirit as soon as ever I saw him.”

label: Quote
value: Anne Shirley said: "Oh, I don’t mean that sort of a name. I mean just a name you gave it yourself. Didn’t you give it a name? May I give it one then? May I call it—let me see—Bonny would do—may I call it Bonny while I’m here? Oh, do let me!"

label: Quote
value: Anne Shirley said: "Pretty well. I imagine a good deal, and that helps to pass the time. Of course, it’s rather lonesome. But then, I may as well get used to that."

label: Quote
value: Anne Shirley said: "I don’t get cross about other things; but I’m so tired of being twitted about my hair and it just makes me boil right over. Do you suppose my hair will really be a handsome auburn when I grow up?"

label: History
value: Aunt Jamesina was named after James.
unit: Aunt Jamesina was named after her father, James, who drowned at sea a month before her birth. In her past, her mother and husband prevented her from wearing a yellow silk dress, and a former suitor never forgave her after she suggested he use a rubber band to train his ears. She raised a daughter who earned an M.A. after learning to cook, and though she prayed for her daughter to become a missionary, she ultimately wished she had not. Aunt Jamesina moved into Patty's Place to serve as an easygoing chaperone for Anne Shirley and her friends, bringing along her pet, the Sarah-cat, which she had received as a gift from her washerwoman Sarah. During her time chaperoning, she conversed with Anne about growing up on Anne's twentieth birthday and offered advice when Anne discussed her options. She later welcomed the girls back to Patty's Place for their final year at Redmond, catching up with them as they unpacked.

label: History
value: Davy Keith was brought to live at Green Gables by Marilla Cuthbert.
unit: Davy Keith and his twin sister, Dora, were brought to live at Green Gables by Marilla Cuthbert. He quickly proved to be a handful, causing trouble by dropping a caterpillar down a girl's neck at church, coaxing Dora into a pigpen before pumping water over her, and hiding a toad in Marilla's bed. Soon after, he trapped Dora in a toolhouse and lied about it, but broke down in remorse when he realized lying was wrong, prompting Anne Shirley and Marilla to educate and discipline him. After being caught stealing plum jam and skipping his prayers to test Marilla, he received reassurance of Anne's affection, though he grew jealous when she paid attention to other children. He also frequently ruined household meals and received scoldings from Marilla over his poor table manners.

label: Quote
value: Davy Keith said: "You don’t look like a lady who’d whip a little boy just ’cause he couldn’t keep still. Didn’t you find it awful hard to keep still when you was only ‘s old as me?"

label: Quote
value: Davy Keith said: "You was a girl once, I s’pose, though it’s awful funny to think of it. Dora can sit still . . . but there ain’t much fun in it I don’t think. Seems to me it must be slow to be a girl. Here, Dora, let me liven you up a bit."

label: Quote
value: Davy Keith said: "Marilla washed it yesterday . . . and Mrs. Wiggins scoured me with hard soap the day of the funeral. That’s enough for one week. I don’t see the good of being so awful clean. It’s lots more comfable being dirty."

label: Quote
value: Davy Keith said: "But it was such a jolly big caterpillar . . . I picked him up on the church steps just as we went in. It seemed a pity to waste him. And say, wasn’t it fun to hear that girl yell?"

value: Davy Keith said: “I . . . did something else today,” went on Davy in a muffled voice. “I’m sorry now but I’m awful scared to tell you. You won’t be very cross, will you? And you won’t tell Marilla, will you?”

label: History
value: Diana Barry was named by a boarding schoolmaster.
unit: When Diana Barry was born, she was named by a boarding schoolmaster, and as a young girl, she belonged to a childhood Story Club. She formed an instant bond with Anne Shirley in her garden, pledging to be her lifelong bosom friend. Soon after, their friendship faced a crisis when Diana's mother temporarily forbade them from playing together after a misunderstanding, leading to a tearful farewell; however, the relationship was restored when Diana sought Anne's help to nurse her sister Minnie May through severe croup. Diana later participated in a successful Christmas concert with Anne and subsequently rushed to Green Gables to deliver the news that Anne had tied for first place on the entrance exam. As they grew older, Diana canvassed for the Avonlea Village Improvement Society alongside Anne, went on picnics where she shared local history, and accompanied Anne on misadventures that included getting stuck in a duck house roof and discovering Echo Lodge. Despite fearing she would be left behind when Anne pursued higher education, Diana became engaged to Fred Wright and later married him at Orchard Slope. Following her marriage, Diana gave birth to a son, little Fred, welcoming Anne to her home to visit her new baby.

label: Quote
value: Diana Barry said: "I’m awfully glad you’ve come to live at Green Gables. It will be jolly to have somebody to play with. There isn’t any other girl who lives near enough to play with, and I’ve no sisters big enough."

label: Quote
value: Diana Barry said: “Yes,” said Diana, tossing her head, “but I’m sure he doesn’t like Julia Bell so very much. I’ve heard him say he studied the multiplication table by her freckles.”

label: Quote
value: Diana Barry said: “Those Pye girls are cheats all round,” said Diana indignantly, as they climbed the fence of the main road. “Gertie Pye actually went and put her milk bottle in my place in the brook yesterday. Did you ever? I don’t speak to her now.”

label: Quote
value: Diana Barry said: "Why, he makes fun of all the girls. He laughs at mine because it’s so black. He’s called me a crow a dozen times; and I never heard him apologize for anything before, either."

label: Quote
value: Diana Barry said: "I do think you’re mean. What shall I do? Mr. Phillips will make me sit with that horrid Gertie Pye—I know he will because she is sitting alone. Do come back, Anne."

label: History
value: Dora was brought to Green Gables.
unit: Dora was brought to Green Gables as an orphan alongside her twin brother, Davy. Soon after arriving, she was pumped over with water by Davy after he lured her into a pigpen, and he later trapped her inside a toolhouse where she was eventually found by Anne Shirley. During her time at school, Dora grew frightened of the dark after hearing ghost stories from Mirabel Cotton, and she was once kissed in school by Frank Bell. Her long-term future at Green Gables was secured after her uncle, Richard Keith, passed away and left money for the twins' care. Later, Davy coerced Dora into skipping Sunday School to play and go fishing with the Cottons.

value: Gilbert Blythe said: ““All right!” Gilbert sprang into his skiff with an angry color in his cheeks. “I’ll never ask you to be friends again, Anne Shirley. And I don’t care either!”

label: Quote
value: Gilbert Blythe said: "It wasn’t particularly good of me at all, Anne. I was pleased to be able to do you some small service. Are we going to be friends after this? Have you really forgiven me my old fault?"

value: Gilbert Blythe said: "We were born to be good friends, Anne. You’ve thwarted destiny enough. I know we can help each other in many ways. You are going to keep up your studies, aren’t you? So am I. Come, I’m going to walk home with you."

Having kept house with his sister until her death, he fulfilled a promise to her by marrying Emily Scott after delaying marriage for a long time. However, following a two-week wedding trip to St. John, the couple separated over issues involving his foul-mouthed parrot, Ginger. In Avonlea, Harrison initially clashed with his neighbor Anne after accusing her cow of ruining his oats, but he warmed to her after she accidentally sold his Jersey cow and came to confess the mistake. Their friendship grew through frequent visits, during which Harrison voiced his doubts about Anne's teaching methods, refused to donate to her village improvement canvass, and accidentally locked Davy's twin, Dora, in his toolhouse. His life took a sharp turn when a severe hail storm destroyed his parrot, Ginger, shortly after which his estranged wife Emily arrived at Green Gables looking for him and the two reconciled. Harrison remained a candid presence in Anne's life, later providing blunt critiques on her fictional story and informing her of a baking powder story contest that Diana secretly submitted Anne's work to win. During a winter holiday, he visited Green Gables once again to deliver the mail to Anne.

When James's dying sailor brother sent him a swearing parrot named Ginger, a conflict over the bird led to his separation from Emily, who left for her own home after demanding he choose between her and the pet.

label: History
value: Jane Andrews attended school.
unit: Jane Andrews attended school and Queen's Academy alongside Anne Shirley and Ruby Gillis, during which she lived in the same boarding house as her Avonlea peers after starting classes at the academy. Prior to attending Queen's, she participated in a dramatic play of Elaine with Anne, Diana, and Ruby. On one occasion, she traveled with Anne and Billy to a benefit concert at the White Sands Hotel, later sharing supper and a ride home with Anne and Diana. Before her first term as a teacher, Jane met with Anne and Gilbert to discuss their different philosophies on teaching and discipline. She later resigned from the Avonlea school with plans to head West, eventually taking up a teaching position on the western prairies. Earlier in her youth, she joined Anne, Diana, and Priscilla on a picnic walk where they discovered the garden of Hester Gray, and she accompanied Anne and Diana to unsuccessfully persuade Judson Parker regarding fence advertisements. While staying overnight in Anne's room, Jane acted as a proxy to propose marriage to Anne on behalf of her brother Billy, leaving Jane somewhat offended when Anne promptly rejected the offer.

label: History
value: Aunt Josephine Barry was a resident of Charlottetown.
unit: Aunt Josephine Barry was a resident of Charlottetown who was initially angered when Anne Shirley and Diana Barry unexpectedly leaped onto her while she was sleeping in a spare-room bed. However, after Anne visited her to apologize, Josephine was won over by her honesty and agreed to forgive Diana. She later hosted Anne and Diana at her mansion for the Exhibition, frequently received Anne at her home during Anne's studies at Queen's Academy, and attended Anne's commencement. Upon her death, Josephine left Anne a bequest of one thousand dollars in her will.

label: History
value: Miss Lavendar Lewis was an eccentric woman.
unit: Miss Lavendar Lewis was an eccentric woman living at Echo Lodge who hired little Charlotta Bowman after her mother died ten years prior. One October, Anne Shirley and Diana Barry stumbled upon Echo Lodge, where Miss Lavendar entertained them with tea and demonstrated the magical echoes of her home, though she was noticeably shaken when Anne mentioned Paul Irving. Miss Lavendar later confided in Anne about her past romance and broken engagement with Paul's father, Stephen Irving, after which Anne brought Paul to meet her. Following a note delivered by Anne, Stephen visited Echo Lodge, leading to their joyful reconciliation and eventual marriage. Time later, during a summer visit from Anne, Miss Lavendar cautioned her that she and Gilbert Blythe were meant for each other.

label: Quote
value: Lavendar Lewis said: "But oh, won’t you stay and have tea with me? Please, do. Mr. Kimball’s will have tea over before you get there. And Charlotta the Fourth and I will be so glad to have you."

label: Quote
value: Lavendar Lewis said: "I love them myself. They are very good company . . . with a little pretending. On calm evenings Charlotta the Fourth and I often sit out here and amuse ourselves with them. Charlotta, take back the horn and hang it carefully in its place."

label: Quote
value: Lavendar Lewis said: "It gave me a shock to hear about Stephen’s son that first day you were here, Anne. I’ve never been able to mention him to you since, but I’ve wanted to know all about him. What sort of a boy is he?"

label: Quote
value: Lavendar Lewis said: "Oh, I’m not so old as I thought . . . and I don’t need a single blue pill! Girls, when you come back with your strawberries we’ll have tea out here under the silver poplar. I’ll have it all ready for you with home-grown cream."

label: Quote
value: Lavendar Lewis said: "I’m wholesomely ashamed to think that a new dress . . . even it is a forget-me-not organdy . . . should exhilarate me so, when a good conscience and an extra contribution to Foreign Missions couldn’t do it."

label: Personality
value: Marilla Cuthbert is sensible.
unit: Sensible, practical, and orderly, Marilla Cuthbert approaches life with a stern and self-contained demeanor, viewing the world purely through prose. In raising a child, she is deeply committed to her duty, believing strongly in moral lessons and striving to drill a tranquil uniformity of disposition into her charge. Though she is critical, strict, and prone to sarcasm after showing vulnerability, she has nevertheless grown more mellow over time. She remains highly undemonstrative, repressed, and reluctant to openly express her deep affection or admit her pride. Beyond her household duties, she is locally celebrated for making homemade currant wine, is skilled at crafting round braided mats, and strongly detests cats.

unit: Marilla Cuthbert lived at Green Gables for sixty years, having spent forty-five of them as neighbors with Rachel Lynde. In her youth, Marilla refused to forgive her suitor John Blythe after a quarrel, resulting in the end of their romance, and she spent the long years of her middle life in dull monotony. Having been raised under the strict rule that children should be seen and not heard, Marilla was shocked when an orphan girl, Anne, was mistakenly sent to Green Gables instead of a boy. Though initially intending to send her back, Marilla took pity on Anne's hard past and agreed to keep and educate her. Over time, despite Anne's dramatic blunders and a false confession regarding Marilla's inherited amethyst brooch, Marilla grew deeply affectionate toward the girl. When severe eye trouble forced Marilla to give up reading and sewing, Anne sacrificed her college scholarship to stay home and save Green Gables. Marilla later agreed to take in her late friend's orphaned twins, Davy and Dora, and she eventually invited the newly widowed Mrs. Lynde to move into Green Gables so Anne could finally attend Redmond College.

label: Quote
value: Marilla Cuthbert said: "I’d never dream of taking a girl to bring up. I wonder at Mrs. Alexander Spencer for doing it. But there, she wouldn’t shrink from adopting a whole orphan asylum if she took it into her head."

label: Quote
value: Marilla Cuthbert said: "I don’t feel as if I wanted any more children to look after than I’ve got at present. You’re problem enough in all conscience. What’s to be done with you I don’t know. Matthew is a most ridiculous man."

label: Quote
value: Marilla Cuthbert said: “There, there, Marilla, you can have your own way,” said Matthew reassuringly. “Only be as good and kind to her as you can without spoiling her. I kind of think she’s one of the sort you can do anything with if you only get her to love you.”

label: Quote
value: Marilla Cuthbert said: "Matthew Cuthbert, I’m astonished at you. You know that Anne’s behavior was dreadful, and yet you take her part! I suppose you’ll be saying next thing that she oughtn’t to be punished at all!"

label: Quote
value: Marilla Cuthbert said: "She’ll have her meals regular, and I’ll carry them up to her myself. But she’ll stay up there until she’s willing to apologize to Mrs. Lynde, and that’s final, Matthew."

label: Personality
value: Matthew Cuthbert is exceptionally quiet.
unit: Matthew Cuthbert is an exceptionally quiet, shy, and unobservant man who hates going among strangers or speaking in public. He harbors a deep dread of women—feeling they secretly laugh at him—and has traditionally felt a mortal dread of little girls, while new acquaintances like a new minister's wife terrify him. Despite his quiet nature, he is a sympathetic listener who enjoys talkative people willing to converse for him. He is also hard-working, patient, wise, and does not seek out excitement. Though argument is not his strong point, he is remarkably persistent and holds fast to his opinions once he takes a whim into his head.

value: Matthew Cuthbert lives at Green Gables.
unit: Matthew Cuthbert lived at Green Gables with his sister, Marilla. Though they originally intended to adopt an orphan boy to help on the farm, Matthew went to the Bright River station and was surprised to find Anne Shirley, a young orphan girl, waiting for him instead. Matthew was quickly charmed by her imaginative chatter and quietly advocated for keeping her at Green Gables. Over the years, he offered her warmth, encouragement, and gifts, such as chocolates and a calf bought from Mr. Bell. He also secretly convinced her to apologize to Mrs. Rachel Lynde to end a punishment and advocated for her to attend a local concert. Seeing that Anne lacked stylish clothes, Matthew arranged with Mrs. Lynde to secretly procure a fashionable dress with puffed sleeves for Anne for Christmas. Later, Matthew and Marilla agreed to support Anne joining an advanced class to prepare for the Queen's Entrance examination. When Anne tied for first place on the exam, she ran to the field to share her triumph with Matthew and her family. Matthew attended Anne's commencement at Queen's Academy when she won the Avery scholarship.

value: Matthew Cuthbert said: "It’ll have to be done sooner or later, you know, for Marilla’s a dreadful determined woman—dreadful determined, Anne. Do it right off, I say, and have it over."

label: Quote
value: Matthew Cuthbert said: "That’s right—that’s right, Anne. But don’t tell Marilla I said anything about it. She might think I was putting my oar in and I promised not to do that."

label: Quote
value: Matthew Cuthbert said: “Well now, you’ll have to punish her,” said Matthew, reaching for his hat. “I’ve nothing to do with it, remember. You warned me off yourself.”

label: History
value: Paul Irving lost his mother three years prior to attending Avonlea school.
unit: Paul Irving, a creative student who once wrote a composition about a moonshine boat, lost his mother three years prior to attending the Avonlea school. On Anne Shirley's first day of teaching, she formed a quick bond with Paul after he gave her flowers, and he soon became her favorite pupil. In his schoolwork, Paul shared his imaginative world of rock people and fantastical journeys to sunset lands. At the end of the school year, he visited the graveyard with Anne to discuss his mother's memory and his life living with his grandmother. After Anne introduced Paul to Miss Lavendar, Paul conversed with her about their shared imaginary dream-people and later visited Echo Lodge as his father prepared to marry her.

label: Quote
value: Paul Irving said: "and I came back to give them to you because I thought you were the kind of lady that would like them, and because . . ."

label: Quote
value: Paul Irving said: “Yes; but if dryads are foolish they must take the consequences, just as if they were real people,” said Paul gravely. “Do you know what I think about the new moon, teacher? I think it is a little golden boat full of dreams.”

label: Quote
value: Paul Irving said: "I’ve eaten enough to make anyone grow. I do hope, now that I’ve begun, I’ll keep on till I’m as tall as father. He is six feet, you know, Miss Lavendar."

label: Quote
value: Paul Irving said: "you can’t think what has happened! Something so splendid. Father is here . . . just think of that! Father is here! Come right in. Father, this is my beautiful teacher. You know, father."

label: Quote
value: Paul Irving said: "I think you would make a splendid mother. You have just the right look in your eyes . . . the look my little mother always had. I think it’s a pity you haven’t any boys of your own."

label: History
value: Philippa Gordon hailed from Bolingbroke, Nova Scotia.
unit: Philippa "Phil" Gordon hailed from Bolingbroke, Nova Scotia, where she belonged to an old, exclusive Bluenose family as the daughter of a rich, well-known man. After registering at Redmond College, she met Anne Shirley and Priscilla Grant in Old St. John's Cemetery and quickly befriended them. When Anne and Priscilla arranged to rent Patty's Place for their second year, Phil begged and received permission to live with them. She later invited Anne to spend a fortnight at her home in Bolingbroke. Over time, Phil fell in love with a theological student named Jonas Blake, and she eventually accepted his marriage proposal after he popped the question. During her final year at Redmond, Phil comforted Anne after Anne rejected a marriage proposal from Royal Gardner.

label: Quote
value: Phil Gordon said: "I’ll go, if I can walk with Priscilla and Charlie. That will be a bearable degree of gooseberry. That Gilbert of yours is a darling, Anne, but why does he go around so much with Goggle-eyes?"

label: Quote
value: Phil Gordon said: "I don’t want William’s Island especially, but I’m sure I couldn’t get it if I did. Look at that sentry on the summit of the fort, right beside the flag. Doesn’t he look as if he had stepped out of a romance?"

label: Quote
value: Phil Gordon said: "Look—in white letters, around the archway over the gate. ‘Patty’s Place.’ Isn’t that killing? Especially on this Avenue of Pinehursts and Elmwolds and Cedarcrofts? ‘Patty’s Place,’ if you please! I adore it."

label: Quote
value: Phil Gordon said: "They really are such dear boys, you know. There’s to be no end of dances and drives and general jamborees. I shall never forgive you, Queen Anne, for not coming home with me for the holidays."

label: Quote
value: Phil Gordon said: "There’ll be one or two quilting parties, I suppose; and all the old gossips will talk you over to your face and behind your back. You’ll die of lonesomeness, child."

label: History
value: Priscilla Grant attended Queen's Academy
unit: Priscilla Grant attended Queen's Academy alongside Anne Shirley. She later joined Anne, Jane, and Diana on a spring picnic walk where they discovered the flower-filled garden of Hester Gray. Afterwards, she sent Anne a letter explaining that author Mrs. Morgan had sprained her ankle, preventing an intended visit; however, Priscilla later unexpectedly arrived at Green Gables with Mrs. Morgan and Mrs. Pendexter, enjoying a pleasant dinner and woodland walk hosted by Anne. The following year, Priscilla greeted Anne in Kingsport and moved into a new boarding house with her. While registering at Redmond College, the pair met and quickly befriended vibrant fellow student Philippa Gordon. During their second term, Priscilla joined Anne in searching for a house to rent for the upcoming school year, successfully arranging to lease Patty's Place from Miss Patty and Miss Maria.

label: Personality
value: Mrs. Rachel Lynde is an exceptionally capable manager.
unit: Mrs. Rachel Lynde is an exceptionally capable, farseeing, and clever manager who handles her own affairs while frequently involving herself in those of others. Notably inquisitive, curious, and observant, she keeps a sharp eye on everything that passes, rarely letting anything escape her notice. Though she can be bossy, critical, and compulsively corrective toward people of all ages, she possesses a kind, generous heart and excels at sewing. She is an outspoken, matter-of-fact, and somewhat gossipy woman who loves giving advice and holds strong opinions, including a prejudice against Yankees and a firm opposition to women's higher education, play-acting, and writing fiction. A tender, patient nurse to her husband, she is also a pessimistic judge of human nature who holds strict religious beliefs.

label: History
value: Mrs. Rachel Lynde had brought up ten children
unit: Mrs. Rachel Lynde had brought up ten children and buried two, married at eighteen, and lived as Marilla Cuthbert's neighbor for forty-five years without a quarrel. Having knitted sixteen cotton warp quilts, she eventually broke up housekeeping to devote more time to church affairs. When Marilla planned to adopt an orphan boy, Rachel strongly disapproved and warned her against the decision. After meeting the young orphan girl, Anne, Rachel offended her with blunt remarks about her red hair, leading to a fiery confrontation; she later completely forgiven Anne after receiving a dramatic apology and gifted her flowers. She went on to advise Marilla to let Anne study at home when she refused to return to school, assisted Matthew in sewing a fashionable dress with puffed sleeves for Anne, and helped Anne win over Aunt Josephine Barry after a blunder at the Barry home. Rachel eventually approved of Anne's growth, joined in praising her entrance examination success, and later provided Marilla with local gossip, reports of Anthony Pye's respect for Anne's teaching, and commentary on community matters. Following the passing of her husband, Thomas Lynde, Rachel moved into Green Gables to live with Marilla, allowing Anne to leave her teaching post for Redmond College. In her new home, she helped establish house rules for the orphaned twins, Davy and Dora, and remained a familiar presence on the porch discussing local events and village gossip.

label: Quote
value: Ruby Gillis said: ““Nor I,” said Ruby Gillis, with a shiver. “I don’t mind floating down when there’s two or three of us in the flat and we can sit up. It’s fun then. But to lie down and pretend I was dead—I just couldn’t. I’d die really of fright.”

label: Quote
value: Ruby Gillis said: "Anne, it won’t be long now before I’ll be lying over there. You and Diana and all the rest will be going about, full of life—and I’ll be there—in the old graveyard—dead!"

label: Quote
value: Ruby Gillis said: "I’ll try. I’ll think over what you have said, and try to believe it. And you’ll come up as often as you can, won’t you, Anne?"

label: Quote
value: Ruby Gillis said: "There’s a concert at Carmody and a party at White Sands. Herb Spencer’s going to take me. He’s my latest. Be sure to come up tomorrow. I’m dying for a good talk with you. I want to hear all about your doings at Redmond."

label: Quote
value: Ruby Gillis said: "Me! Why, I’m perfectly well. I never felt better in my life. Of course, that congestion last winter pulled me down a little. But just see my color. I don’t look much like an invalid, I’m sure."

label: History
value: Shirley was born in Bolingbroke, Nova Scotia.
unit: Shirley was born in Bolingbroke, Nova Scotia, and spent her early childhood as an orphan experiencing hard labor with Mrs. Thomas and Mrs. Hammond before being placed in an asylum. While being driven down the shore road toward White Sands, Shirley shared the history of her childhood with Marilla, whose pity was stirred by Shirley's starved life. Later, while attending the Queen's Academy commencement with Marilla, Matthew, and Aunt Josephine, Shirley won the Avery scholarship. During a summer vacation in Avonlea spent feeling lonely over her strained friendship with Gilbert, Shirley enjoyed visits with Paul, Priscilla, Charlotta, and Miss Lavendar. While walking in the park during a rainstorm, Shirley was rescued by Royal Gardner, who walked her back to Patty's Place and subsequently sent her roses.

label: Quote
value: Shirley said: "Fare thee well, my beloved friend. Henceforth we must be as strangers though living side by side. But my heart will ever be faithful to thee."

label: Quote
value: Shirley said: “I’m going back to school,” she announced. “That is all there is left in life for me, now that my friend has been ruthlessly torn from me. In school I can look at her and muse over days departed.”

label: Quote
value: Shirley said: “I think he has only been its nominal head for many years,” said Anne. “He is a very old man; his nephews are really at the head of the institution.”

label: Quote
value: Shirley said: “If I had been the boy you sent for,” said Anne wistfully, “I’d be able to help you so much now and spare you in a hundred ways. I could find it in my heart to wish I had been, just for that.”

label: Quote
value: Shirley said: "I know by experience that it’s very unpleasant to have one’s name spelled wrong and I suppose it must be even worse to have it pronounced wrong."

label: Gilbert Blythe
value: Anne and Gilbert built their relationship.
unit: Anne and Gilbert initially built their relationship on an intense academic rivalry during their school years and at Queen's Academy. Over time, their dynamic softened into friendship, marked by brief moments of romantic tension such as when they tidied Echo Lodge together after a wedding. After learning that Gilbert is critically ill with typhoid fever, Anne suffers through a night of vigil and comes to the sudden realization that she loves him and always has.

label: Quote
value: Stella Maynard said: "I was afraid they’d come back. And then our jolly little nest here would be broken up—and we poor callow nestlings thrown out on the cruel world of boardinghouses again."

label: Quote
value: Stella Maynard said: "I love Anne and I like Roy. Everybody says she is making a brilliant match, and even Mrs. Gardner thinks her charming now. It all sounds as if it were made in heaven, but I have my doubts. Make the most of that, Aunt Jamesina."

label: Quote
value: Stella Maynard said: "Nothing seems worthwhile. My very thoughts are old. I’ve thought them all before. What is the use of living after all, Anne?"

label: Quote
value: Stella Maynard said: "Oh, my mind agrees with you, Anne. But my soul remains doleful and uninspired. I’m always grubby and dingy on rainy nights."

label: Quote
value: Stella Maynard said: "I begin to feel that life is worth living as long as there’s a laugh in it."

To Anne's surprise, the punishment earns Anthony's respect, as later confirmed when he behaves pleasantly and Mrs. Rachel Lynde shares his approval.

To Anne's surprise, the punishment earns Anthony's respect, as later confirmed when he behaves pleasantly and Mrs. Rachel Lynde shares his approval.

label: v2 · XII A Jonah Day
value: Anne has a miserable mood caused by a toothache.
chapter: v2 · XII A Jonah Day
unit: In a miserable mood caused by a toothache, Anne has a terrible day at school, accidentally causing firecrackers to explode in the stove and losing her temper enough to whip Anthony Pye for putting a mouse in her desk. That evening, Marilla comforts a remorseful Anne at Green Gables. To Anne's surprise, the punishment earns Anthony's respect, as later confirmed when he behaves pleasantly and Mrs. Rachel Lynde shares his approval.

label: v2 · XIII A Golden Picnic
value: Anne invites Diana.
chapter: v2 · XIII A Golden Picnic
unit: Anne invites Diana to celebrate her spring "adopted birthday" with a picnic walk through the woods with Jane and Priscilla. On Saturday, the four girls explore new paths, name a woodland pool "Crystal Lake," and discover the forgotten, flower-filled garden of Hester Gray. Sitting among the narcissi, Diana shares the poignant story of Hester's life and death, which deeply touches Anne.

unit: Anne tearfully explains to Marilla that Mrs. Barry accused her of making Diana drunk, prompting Marilla to check the pantry and realize Anne mistakenly served currant wine instead of raspberry cordial. A distraught Anne returns to Green Gables, and Marilla quietly softens with sympathy as she checks on the sleeping child later that night.

chapter: v1 · CHAPTER XXIII. Anne Comes to Grief in an Affair of Honor
unit: At Diana's party, Josie Pye dares Anne to walk the ridgepole of Mr. Barry's kitchen roof. Anne attempts the dare, loses her balance, and falls, breaking her ankle. chapter: v2 · VIII Marilla Adopts Twins
unit: Marilla brings the orphaned twins, Davy and Dora, to Green Gables. Davy quickly proves to be a handful, getting into trouble by dropping a caterpillar down a girl's neck in church and pumping water over Dora after coaxing her into a pigpen. Anne attempts to gently guide Davy while removing a toad he hid in Marilla's bed.

unit: Anne discusses Mrs. Lynde and the village hall project with Mr. Harrison. The news spreads, devastating the Village Improvement Society, but the villagers rally behind the young people while blaming the Pyes for the mistake.

label: v2 · XII A Jonah Day
value: Anne has a miserable mood caused by a toothache.
chapter: v2 · XII A Jonah Day
unit: In a miserable mood caused by a toothache, Anne has a terrible day at school, accidentally causing firecrackers to explode in the stove and losing her temper enough to whip Anthony Pye for putting a mouse in her desk. That evening, Marilla comforts a remorseful Anne at Green Gables. To Anne's surprise, the punishment earns Anthony's respect, as later confirmed when he behaves pleasantly and Mrs. Rachel Lynde shares his approval.

chapter: v2 · XIV A Danger Averted
unit: Anne catches Davy stealing plum jam and lectures him, before learning with Marilla that the twins will remain at Green Gables until fall. Later at an Improvers meeting, Gertie Pye announces that Judson Parker plans to rent his fence to a patent-medicine company for advertisements. Anne, Jane, and Diana visit Judson to persuade him otherwise, but he smoothly refuses to change his mind.

Anne attempts to gently guide Davy while removing a toad he hid in Marilla's bed.

unit: In a miserable mood caused by a toothache, Anne has a terrible day at school, accidentally causing firecrackers to explode in the stove and losing her temper enough to whip Anthony Pye for putting a mouse in her desk. That evening, Marilla comforts a remorseful Anne at Green Gables. To Anne's surprise, the punishment earns Anthony's respect, as later confirmed when he behaves pleasantly and Mrs. Rachel Lynde shares his approval.

chapter: v2 · XIV A Danger Averted
unit: Anne catches Davy stealing plum jam and lectures him, before learning with Marilla that the twins will remain at Green Gables until fall. Later at an Improvers meeting, Gertie Pye announces that Judson Parker plans to rent his fence to a patent-medicine company for advertisements. Anne, Jane, and Diana visit Judson to persuade him otherwise, but he smoothly refuses to change his mind.

unit: Anne puts Davy to bed after answering his curious questions about sleep and jam. unit: Marilla leaves Green Gables for town with Dora while Davy goes off with Mr. Harrison, leaving Anne to do chores. unit: Anne catches Davy stealing plum jam and lectures him, before learning with Marilla that the twins will remain at Green Gables until fall. Later at an Improvers meeting, Gertie Pye announces that Judson Parker plans to rent his fence to a patent-medicine company for advertisements. Anne, Jane, and Diana visit Judson to persuade him otherwise, but he smoothly refuses to change his mind.

To Anne's surprise, the punishment earns Anthony's respect, as later confirmed when he behaves pleasantly and Mrs. Rachel Lynde shares his approval.

A letter from Priscilla later explains that Mrs. Morgan sprained her ankle, leaving Anne disappointed but resilient.

chapter: v2 · VIII Marilla Adopts Twins
unit: Marilla brings the orphaned twins, Davy and Dora, to Green Gables. unit: Noticing that Anne lacks stylish clothes like her schoolmates, Matthew decides to give her a fashionable dress for Christmas.
